name: ui-lib
description: React component library. Next.js, TypeScript, CSS variables + CSS Modules. Controls are built on Base UI.
principles: HTML first: use the semantic element for the job. Own components render correct HTML; Base UI components handle behavior and ARIA.
Use semantic tokens only; never hardcode colors, spacing or fonts.
Every control needs an accessible name: Field `label`, the component's `label`/`legend`, or `aria-label`.
One way to do each thing: links are Link, actions are Button, headings are Heading, body text is Text.
Keep heading levels in order, one h1 per page.

components.name: Text
components.description:
Body-level text: paragraphs, labels, captions and inline code.
For headings use `Heading`; for links use `Link`.
components.renders: p (body variants), span (label, caption), code (code); or the element in `as`
components.composition: `as` accepts only: p, span, label, strong, em, small, div, code. No links or buttons.
components.whenToUse: Any paragraph, label, caption or inline code that is not a heading. Small styles: `label` for controls (buttons, tabs); `body-sm` for secondary reading text (descriptions, helper text); `caption` for metadata (timestamps, counters, footnotes).
avoid: Headings: use Heading.
Links: use Link.
Actions: use Button.
Setting font-size or color by hand.
Caption size="sm" (10px) for lowercase running text: it is intentional for uppercase metadata, where the extra tracking keeps it legible.
Form labels: use Label, or Field when you also need description and error.
components.accessibility: Do not use tone="subtle" for required text.

props.name: as
props.description:
HTML element to render. Defaults by variant: `p` for body variants, `span` for
`label` and `caption`, `code` for `code`.

props.name: casing
props.description: Set to `uppercase` for small uppercase captions.

props.name: size
props.description:
Size within the variant: body is 18px (`lg`), 15px (`base`) or 13px (`sm`); caption is 12px, 11px or 10px;
code is 14px (`base`), 13px (`sm`) or 12px (`xs`). Ignored by `label` and `emphasis`.

props.name: tone
props.description: Text color from the semantic color tokens.

props.name: variant
props.description: Which text style to apply. Appearance only; it does not change the element.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight. Only three exist; there is no light. Defaults to the variant's own weight.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Text>Default paragraph.</Text>
<Text size="lg">Large body text</Text>
<Text variant="caption" tone="muted">Helper text</Text>

components.name: Heading
components.description:
A heading. Separates semantics (`as`) from appearance (`size`). Headings are always upright and semibold.
When `id` is omitted, a stable slug of the text is used, so anchors render the same on the server and the client.
components.renders: h1-h6 from `as` (default h2)
components.composition: `as` sets the outline level (h1-h6 only); `size` sets only the look.
components.whenToUse: Page and section titles.
avoid: Skipping levels (h1 then h3).
More than one h1 per page.
Choosing a level for its look: change `size` instead.
components.accessibility: Heading order is part of the page structure for screen reader users.

props.name: as
props.description: Heading level in the document outline. Keep one `h1` per page and do not skip levels.

props.name: size
props.description:
Visual size from 1 (56px) to 6 (20px) on wide screens. Defaults to the size that matches `as`.
Use it to get an `h2` that looks like a size 4.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight. There is no light; headings are semibold unless you set another.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Heading as="h1">Page title</Heading>
<Heading as="h2" size={4}>Smaller-looking section title</Heading>

components.name: Link
components.description:
A link for navigation. It renders an `a`, or the component given to `LinkProvider` (such as `next/link`).
Links with a label always show an underline so they do not rely on color alone. For actions that do not navigate, use `Button`.
Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon`. An icon on its own is a valid link (`startIcon` + `aria-label`).
components.renders: a
components.composition: Native anchor props pass through. `href` is required. Put a trailing icon in `endIcon` (no `size`). Set `standalone` for a link used as a standalone action; inline links in a sentence stay inline.
components.whenToUse: Navigation to another page, section or resource.
avoid: Actions that do not navigate: use Button.
Links without visible text.
Button-styled navigation: use ButtonLink.
components.accessibility: Always underlined so it does not rely on color (the underline gets stronger on hover). Use `target="_blank"` only with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes. Required: a link without `href` is not a link.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the link sizes it.

props.name: standalone
props.description: Marks a standalone action link (not inline in a sentence) so it gets a 44px hit area on touch devices.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the link sizes it.

props.name: tone
props.description: `default` uses the text color, `muted` the secondary text color, `inherit` the surrounding color. The underline is always there.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Link href="/docs">Read the docs</Link>
<Link href="/docs" endIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />}>Read the docs</Link>
<Link href="/next" aria-label="Next page" startIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />} />

components.name: Kbd
components.description: A keyboard key or shortcut. Renders a native `kbd`. Use one `Kbd` per key and join keys with text.
components.renders: kbd
components.composition: One Kbd per key; join keys with text such as +.
components.whenToUse: Keyboard shortcuts in docs and UI.
avoid: Using it as a button.
components.accessibility: Native kbd semantics. Spell out symbols that screen readers read poorly, for example add VisuallyHidden text.
components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Kbd>⌘</Kbd> + <Kbd>K</Kbd>

components.name: Badge
components.description:
Small status, category or count label. Text is always the primary signal; the
variant only reinforces it.

Keep the text to one or two words and truncate counts to two digits (`99+`).
Badges are secondary and supportive: never use one as a heading or a key
indicator. Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon`; they follow the badge size: sm 16px, md 20px,
lg 24px.
components.renders: span, or the element passed in `render`
components.composition: Text children, plus optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`); never put icons in children. `loading` adds a spinner (`spinnerPosition`: start or end). `variant`: default, inverted, outline, brand, success or danger. `size`: sm, md or lg. Icons follow the size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. `shape`: pill (default) or rounded. Pass `render={<Link href="…" />}` to render a link. Keep text to one or two words; truncate counts to two digits (`99+`).
components.whenToUse: Short status or count labels next to other content.
avoid: Using color as the only signal: always include text.
Badges as headings or key indicators: they are secondary and supportive.
Long descriptions, or mixing different badge sizes side by side.
Styling a badge like a button when it acts as one: use Button.
components.accessibility: Meaning must be in the text; the variant only reinforces it. A badge rendered as a link keeps the link's own accessible name.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the badge sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner before or after the text, for statuses still in progress.

props.name: render
props.description:
Renders the badge as another element or component, e.g. a link:
`render={<Link href="/docs" />}`. Keyboard and focus behavior then come from
that element, since Base UI merges the props.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner shape: `pill` (fully round) or `rounded` (small radius).

props.name: size
props.description: Height and type scale: `sm` 20px, `md` 24px, `lg` 28px.

props.name: spinnerPosition
props.description: Side the spinner sits on.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the badge sizes it.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual treatment. `default` is a quiet component surface, `inverted` a filled
high-contrast pill, `outline` only an inset ring, and `brand`, `success` and
`danger` are soft semantic tints (translucent background, colored text).

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Badge>Draft</Badge>
<Badge variant="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge variant="danger">99+</Badge>
<Badge variant="outline" shape="rounded">Beta</Badge>
<Badge variant="brand" loading>Saving</Badge>
<Badge variant="inverted" size="lg" spinnerPosition="end" loading>Syncing</Badge>
<Badge variant="success" startIcon={<CheckIcon />}>Active</Badge>
<Badge variant="default" render={<Link href="/docs" />}>Docs</Badge>

components.name: Stack
components.description:
One-dimensional layout: children in a row or column with a token-based gap.

`direction` and `gap` accept a per-breakpoint object. Breakpoints are mobile-first:
`sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem, `xl` 80rem. A missing breakpoint inherits the
smaller one, so `{ md: "row" }` stays `column` below 48rem.
components.renders: div (or `as`) with display:flex
components.composition: `as="ul"` or `"ol"` requires `li` children.
components.whenToUse: Arranging children in one direction with a consistent gap.
avoid: Two-dimensional layouts: use Grid.
Margins between children: use `gap`.
components.accessibility: List semantics are restored with role="list" because removing markers drops them in some screen readers.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment on the cross axis.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. With `ul` or `ol`, children must be `li` elements.

props.name: direction
props.description:
Main axis. `column` stacks vertically. Pass a per-breakpoint object to change it responsively;
mobile-first, a missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.

props.name: gap
props.description:
Space between children, from the spacing scale. Pass a per-breakpoint object to change it
responsively; mobile-first, a missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.

props.name: justify
props.description: Distribution on the main axis.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Lets children wrap onto new lines.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
Title Body
  • One
  • Two
    •  One Two

components.name: Grid
components.description:
Two-dimensional layout using CSS grid with a token-based gap.

Breakpoints are mobile-first: `sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem, `xl` 80rem.
A missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.
components.renders: div (or `as`) with display:grid
components.composition: `columns` is a number (equal columns), a full grid-template-columns string, or a per-breakpoint object. `minColumnWidth` uses automatic columns and overrides `columns`.
components.whenToUse: Two-dimensional layouts and card grids.
avoid: One-dimensional layouts: use Stack.
components.accessibility: Visual order should match DOM order.
choosing: Cards, tiles and galleries: use `minColumnWidth` (for example `"16rem"`). Columns fit automatically, with no breakpoints.
Fixed layouts that change by screen (sidebar plus content, 1/2/3 columns): use the responsive `columns` object, for example `{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }`.
Unequal columns: pass a string such as `"2fr 1fr"`, optionally per breakpoint, for example `{ base: 1, lg: "2fr 1fr" }`.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of items inside their cells on the block axis.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. With `ul` or `ol`, children must be `li` elements.

props.name: columnGap
props.description: Column gap override.

props.name: columns
gap
props.description:
Space between rows and columns, from the spacing scale. Pass a per-breakpoint object
to change it responsively; mobile-first, a missing breakpoint inherits the smaller one.

props.name: minColumnWidth
props.description:
Minimum width for automatic columns, for example `"16rem"`. Uses `auto-fit` with no
breakpoints and overrides `columns`. `min(100%, X)` prevents overflow on narrow screens.

props.name: rowGap
props.description: Row gap override.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Grid columns={3} gap="4">...</Grid>
<Grid columns="2fr 1fr">...</Grid>
<Grid minColumnWidth="16rem" gap="4">...</Grid>
<Grid columns={{ base: 1, md: 2, lg: 4 }} gap={{ base: "3", md: "6" }}>...</Grid>
<Grid columns={{ base: 1, lg: "2fr 1fr" }}>...</Grid>

components.name: Container
components.description:
Centers content and limits its width, with side padding from the spacing scale.
The maximum width applies to the content, not to the padding.
components.renders: div (or `as`), centered with a max width
components.composition: `size` is one of sm, md, lg, xl (container tokens) and limits the content width, not the padding. `padding` uses the spacing scale.
components.whenToUse: Page-level width limit and side padding.
avoid: Nesting containers.
Full-width sections: put the background on the section and the Container inside it.
components.accessibility: Use `as="main"` once per page for the primary content.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. Use `main` once per page for the primary content.

props.name: padding
props.description: Side padding from the spacing scale. Override `--container-padding` for a custom value.

props.name: size
props.description: Maximum content width: `sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem, `xl` 80rem.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Container as="main" size="md">...</Container>
<Container size="lg" padding="4">...</Container>

components.name: AspectRatio
components.description:
Reserves space for media with the CSS `aspect-ratio` property. An `img`, `video` or `iframe`
as a direct child fills the box; images and videos use `object-fit: cover`.
components.renders: div by default; `as` can be figure
components.composition: `ratio` is width divided by height (`16 / 9`, `4 / 3`, `1`) and defaults to 1. An `img`, `video` or `iframe` as a direct child fills the box; images and videos use `object-fit: cover`.
components.whenToUse: Images, video, embeds or maps whose size must be reserved before they load, preventing layout shift (CLS).
avoid: Decorative containers with no media.
Text blocks: they size to their content, not a fixed ratio.
components.accessibility: The child needs its own alt text (`img`) or title (`iframe`, `video`); the box adds no semantics.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. Use `figure` when the media needs a caption.

props.name: ratio
props.description:
Width divided by height, such as `16 / 9`, `4 / 3` or `1`. The box reserves that area
before the media loads, which prevents layout shift.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.description:
Hides content visually but keeps it in the accessibility tree, so screen readers still read it.
Never use `display: none` or `aria-hidden` for this purpose.
components.renders: span (or div)
components.composition: Children only.
components.whenToUse: Text that screen readers must read but sighted users should not see, such as the name of an icon-only button.
avoid: display:none or aria-hidden for this purpose: they remove the content from the accessibility tree.
components.accessibility: Stays in the accessibility tree by design.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <button><Icon .../><VisuallyHidden>Close</VisuallyHidden></button>

components.name: Icon
components.description:
Container for a Phosphor glyph (256x256 grid, filled shapes, `currentColor`).
Do not use it with hand-written paths: import a named icon (`ArrowRightIcon`) instead.
components.renders: svg on a 256x256 viewBox, filled with currentColor
components.composition: Do not pass paths. Import a named icon from the set (CheckIcon, ArrowRightIcon ...) generated by `bun run icons` and listed in /agent/icons.json. Each icon takes `size` (sm 16, md 20, lg 24, xl 32) and `weight` (regular | fill).
components.whenToUse: Any glyph. Named icons are decorative by default; pass `label` when the icon is the only carrier of meaning.
avoid: Hand-written <path> children: every icon comes from the generated set.
Meaningful icons without a label.
weight="fill" unless it marks an active or selected state.
components.accessibility: Without `label` it is aria-hidden. With `label` it is role="img" with that name.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name. Provide it when the icon carries meaning on its own (no visible text next to it).
Without `label` the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

props.name: size
props.description:
Fixed size: `sm` 16px, `md` 20px, `lg` 24px, `xl` 32px. Without it the icon is 20px,
or the size its parent sets (inside a `Button` it follows the button).

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Icon label="Success">{glyph}</Icon>

components.name: Spinner
components.description:
Indeterminate loading indicator. Announces `label` through a status region. An empty label makes
it decorative: no status role, no hidden text, and `aria-hidden="true"`.
Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` by slowing the spin instead of stopping it.
components.renders: span with role="status" containing an svg and VisuallyHidden text, or an aria-hidden span when the label is empty
components.composition: No children. Use `label` to describe what is loading. An empty label makes it decorative and silent.
components.whenToUse: Indeterminate loading of an action or small region.
avoid: Several spinners announcing at once.
Page-level loading of content shape: use Skeleton.
components.accessibility: Announces `label` through a status live region; with an empty label it renders no status role, no VisuallyHidden text and aria-hidden="true". Motion follows prefers-reduced-motion.

props.name: label
props.description: Text announced to screen readers.

props.name: size
props.description: Size relative to the surrounding text.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Spinner label="Saving changes" />
<Spinner label="" />

components.name: Skeleton
components.description:
Placeholder for content that is loading. Purely decorative: it is hidden from assistive technology.
Mark the region that is loading with `aria-busy="true"` on its container and announce completion yourself.
components.renders: span (aria-hidden)
components.composition: Shape is text, rect or circle; set width and height with CSS values.
components.whenToUse: Placeholder for content whose layout is known while it loads.
avoid: Using it as the only loading signal.
components.accessibility: Hidden from assistive technology. Put aria-busy="true" on the container that is loading.

props.name: height
props.description: CSS height. Defaults depend on `shape`.

props.name: shape
props.description: Shape of the placeholder. `text` matches one line of body text.

props.name: width
props.description: CSS width, for example `"12rem"` or `"100%"`.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <section aria-busy="true"><Skeleton width="60%" /><Skeleton shape="rect" height="8rem" /></section>

components.name: Button
components.description:
Displays an action button. It is built on Base UI Button, so keyboard, focus and disabled behavior come from there.
It defaults to `type="button"` so it never submits a form by accident; set `type="submit"` explicitly.
For navigation use `ButtonLink` or `Link`.
Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon`. They follow the control size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
An icon-only button is valid only with `startIcon` and an accessible name (`aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`); with visible children both icons are optional.
components.renders: button
components.composition: Defaults to type="button"; pass type="submit" explicitly. Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). Icon-only: `startIcon` is required and exactly one of `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Heights: sm 1.75rem, md 2.25rem, lg 2.75rem. Icons follow the size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Base UI props such as `render` and `nativeButton` are available but not needed for normal use.
components.whenToUse: Any action: submit, open, confirm, cancel. Pass `loading` while the action runs.
avoid: Navigation: use Link (inline text) or ButtonLink (looks like a button).
More than one primary button per view.
Disabling the button to show progress: use `loading`, it keeps the label and focus.
components.accessibility: Icon-only buttons need `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) and use `startIcon` instead of children; the types enforce it. `loading` sets `aria-busy` and counts as the start slot, and the spinner stays silent so the button's accessible name is the only announcement. Keyboard and disabled behavior come from Base UI.

props.name: children
props.description:
The visible label.
Icon-only buttons have no visible children.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the button sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a spinner and ignores clicks while an action is running. The button keeps its label and stays
focusable, and `aria-busy` tells assistive technology it is working.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem, `lg` 2.75rem.

props.name: startIcon
props.description:
Icon before the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the button sizes it.
The visible icon and accessible name. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: variant
props.description:
Visual emphasis. `primary` is the main action (one per view), `secondary` for other actions,
`outline` for a transparent button with a visible border, `ghost` for low-emphasis actions,
`accent` for brand emphasis, `danger` for destructive actions.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Button>Save</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="outline">Learn more</Button>
<Button type="submit">Send</Button>
<Button loading>Saving</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" startIcon={<CheckIcon />}>Done</Button>
<Button variant="outline" aria-label="Close" startIcon={<XIcon />} />

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.description:
Joins related buttons into one control. Shared edges, outer-only corner rounding and a focus
ring that stays above its neighbours keep the actions readable as a unit. Children can be
`Button`, a `Menu` trigger or an `Input` for split-button patterns. Give the group an
`aria-label` so its purpose is announced.
components.renders: div role="group"
components.composition: Pass `orientation` (horizontal or vertical, default horizontal) and one group of related children: `Button`, a `Menu` trigger or an `Input`. Put `ButtonGroupSeparator` between non-outline buttons. Give the group an `aria-label` that names the set of actions.
components.whenToUse: Related actions that belong together and read better as one unit, such as Save draft, Preview and Publish.
avoid: Toggling state or choosing between options: use ToggleGroup.
Unrelated actions that do not form a set.
components.accessibility: Renders role="group"; recommend an `aria-label` so the group is announced. Each child keeps its own accessible name and focus ring, which stays above its neighbours.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
Direction the group lays out its children. Horizontal joins buttons side by side;
vertical stacks them.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Document actions">
  <Button variant="outline">Save draft</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Preview</Button>
  <Button variant="outline">Publish</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

parts.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
parts.description:
Divides adjacent buttons in a group. Use it with non-outline variants, whose shared edge has
no visible border; outline buttons already show the division. The orientation describes the
line itself, so a horizontal group uses a vertical separator.
parts.composition: Place between adjacent buttons when their variants have no visible border. `orientation` describes the line: vertical inside a horizontal group (default), horizontal inside a vertical group.
parts.whenToUse: Marking the division between non-outline buttons in a ButtonGroup.
avoid: Separating outline buttons: their shared border already shows the division.
Using it as decoration outside a ButtonGroup.
parts.accessibility: Exposes role="separator" with an `aria-orientation` that matches the line.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
Direction of the divider line. Use `vertical` between side-by-side buttons (default) and
`horizontal` between stacked buttons.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ButtonGroup aria-label="Export">
  <Button variant="secondary">CSV</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">JSON</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button variant="secondary">More</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

components.name: Field
components.description:
Wraps one control with its label, description and error, wired for accessibility by Base UI Field
(`label` association, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`). Pass `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and
`loading` here; never wire `aria-describedby` or show a loose red error text by hand. When the
control renders its own label or legend, omit `label`; the control prints Required and keeps its
accessible name.

Errors are shown after the field is blurred or the form is submitted, not on the first keystroke.
components.renders: div containing an optional label, the control, a description and an error
components.composition: Wrap one control: Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch or Slider. `label` is optional: omit it when the control renders its own label or legend (Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider). Pass `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` to Field instead of wiring the control. Controls that carry their own label or legend also accept these props directly.
components.whenToUse: Every form control, including its validation, required, read-only and loading states.
avoid: A loose red error text below the control: use Field `error`.
Wiring aria-describedby or aria-invalid by hand.
components.accessibility: Base UI wires the label, aria-describedby and aria-invalid; the error is announced politely. `required` sets the native/ARIA required state and prints Required next to the label, or in the control's own label when Field has no label. Errors show after blur or submit, not on the first keystroke (validationMode defaults to onBlur).

props.name: children
props.description:
The control: `Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch` or `Slider`.
Controls that carry their own label or legend also accept these validation props directly.

props.name: description
props.description: Help text shown under the control and linked with `aria-describedby`.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. When set, the field is marked invalid and the message is linked to the control.
Pass an empty string when there is no error. Show it from validation that runs on blur or submit,
not on the first keystroke (Field defaults to `validationMode="onBlur"`).

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label. Required unless the control renders its own label or legend
(Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch, Slider).

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a small spinner at the end of the control, marks it `aria-busy`, and makes it not editable.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
Makes the control read-only: sunken background, no hover, text not dimmed, still focusable and
selectable. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
Marks the control as required and prints "Required" next to the label. The control also gets
`required` so browsers and assistive technology enforce it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Email" description="We never share it." error={errors.email} required>
  <Input type="email" autoComplete="email" />
</Field>
<Field label="API key" readOnly>
  <Input defaultValue="sk-live-…" />
</Field>
<Field label="Tax ID" loading>
  <Input />
</Field>
<Field error="Turn this on to continue" required>
  <Switch label="Notifications" />
</Field>

components.name: Input
components.description:
A native text input built on Base UI Input. Inside `Field` it is labelled and wired to its
description and error automatically, and it inherits `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
Outside `Field` it needs an accessible name (`aria-label` or an associated `label`).
Icons follow the control size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
components.renders: input
components.composition: Native input props pass through (type, autoComplete, name, required...). Put decorative icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Icons follow the size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
components.whenToUse: Single-line text entry, read-only values and values that are still loading.
avoid: Using it without Field or aria-label.
Multi-line text: use Textarea.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
components.accessibility: Needs an accessible name. Set `autoComplete` for personal data fields. readOnly stays focusable and selectable; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the input sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner at the end and makes the input not editable. `aria-busy` is set.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem, `lg` 2.75rem.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the input sizes it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Email"><Input type="email" autoComplete="email" /></Field>
<Input aria-label="Search" startIcon={<MagnifyingGlassIcon />} />
<Field label="Tax ID" loading><Input /></Field>

components.name: Textarea
components.description:
A native `textarea` that works with `Field` the same way `Input` does, including
`required`, `readOnly` and `loading`. Needs an accessible name inside or outside `Field`.
Icons use the 20px medium size (the textarea has no size variants).
components.renders: textarea
components.composition: Native textarea props pass through; `rows` defaults to 3. Put decorative icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
components.whenToUse: Multi-line text entry, including read-only and loading values.
avoid: Using it without Field or aria-label.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
components.accessibility: Needs an accessible name. readOnly stays focusable and selectable; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the textarea sizes it.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner at the end and makes the textarea not editable. `aria-busy` is set.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the text. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the textarea sizes it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Field label="Message"><Textarea rows={4} /></Field>
<Field label="Notes" readOnly><Textarea defaultValue="Locked for review." /></Field>

components.name: Checkbox
components.description:
A checkbox with its label, built on Base UI Checkbox (keyboard, focus, form value and
indeterminate state come from there). The whole label is clickable. Inside `Field` it
inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: span role="checkbox" with a hidden native input, inside a label
components.composition: `label` is required. Use `indeterminate` for a partial parent state. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
components.whenToUse: Independent yes/no choices, especially ones submitted with a form.
avoid: Mutually exclusive options: use RadioGroup.
Settings that apply instantly: use Switch.
components.accessibility: The whole label is clickable. Base UI handles keyboard and the mixed state. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and uses the sunken background; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, rendered next to the box. Required: every control needs an accessible name.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the checkbox invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the label, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the checkbox not
interactive.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The checkbox can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken background and keeps
the label text at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The checkbox must be ticked before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Checkbox label="Send me product updates" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Select all" indeterminate />
<Checkbox label="Accept terms" error="You must accept the terms" required />

components.name: RadioGroup
components.description:
A group of mutually exclusive options. Renders a `fieldset` with a `legend`, driven by Base UI
RadioGroup. Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: fieldset with a legend and a radiogroup
components.composition: `legend` is required. Children are Radio elements. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field; required prints Required in the legend. Radio is documented under Parts.
components.whenToUse: Choosing exactly one option from a short list.
avoid: Long lists: use Select.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys move the selection. The legend names the group. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Radio` options.

props.name: legend
props.description: Visible group label, rendered as the `legend` of a `fieldset`. Required: the group needs a name.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the group invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the legend, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the group not
interactive.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout of the options.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The group can be focused and read but not changed. Keeps the options at full contrast.
Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The group must have a selection before the form can be submitted. The legend prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<RadioGroup legend="Plan" defaultValue="free">
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>
<RadioGroup legend="Plan" error="Choose a plan" required>
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
</RadioGroup>

parts.name: Radio
parts.description:
One option inside a `RadioGroup`, built on Base UI Radio. The whole label is clickable.
Validation state comes from the `RadioGroup` (`error`, `required`, `readOnly`, `loading`).
parts.renders: span role="radio" with a hidden native input, inside a label
parts.composition: Only inside RadioGroup; it is documented under Parts. `value` and `label` are required.
avoid: Using it outside a RadioGroup.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label for this option.

props.name: value
props.description: Value submitted and reported when this option is selected.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Switch
components.description:
An on/off switch for a setting that applies immediately, built on Base UI Switch.
For choices that are submitted with a form, prefer `Checkbox`. Inside `Field` it inherits
`error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: span role="switch" with a hidden native input, inside a label
components.composition: `label` is required. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
components.whenToUse: A setting that turns on or off immediately.
avoid: Choices that need a Save button: use Checkbox.
components.accessibility: Announced as a switch with on/off state. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and uses the sunken background; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, rendered next to the switch. Required: every control needs an accessible name.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the switch invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the label, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the switch not
interactive.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The switch can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken background when off and
keeps the label text at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The switch must be on before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Switch label="Dark mode" />
<Switch label="Notifications" error="Turn on notifications to continue" required />

components.name: Select
components.description:
A custom select, built on Base UI Select (keyboard, typeahead, focus and form value come from there).
Pass `items` instead of composing parts. Inside `Field` it inherits `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
Icons follow the trigger size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
components.renders: button role="combobox" with a listbox popup in a portal
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, disabled? }), optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`), and give it `label`, `aria-label` or wrap it in Field. `loading` replaces the end icon with a spinner. Icons follow the trigger size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px. Inside Field, omit required/readOnly/loading and pass them to Field.
components.whenToUse: Choosing one option from a longer list, including read-only and loading states.
avoid: Two or three options: use RadioGroup.
Free text: use Input.
Hand-wiring validation ARIA: use Field error.
components.accessibility: Keyboard, typeahead and focus come from Base UI. Needs an accessible name. readOnly prevents choosing another option; loading is readOnly with aria-busy=true.

props.name: items
props.description: The options. Each has a machine `value` and a visible `label`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

props.name: data-force
props.description: Story/test hook: force the focus ring without moving focus.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the value, before the caret. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the select sizes it.

props.name: label
props.description:
Visible label. Provide it, or `aria-label`, or put the Select inside `Field`:
every control needs an accessible name.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner at the end and makes the select not editable. `aria-busy` is set.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `loading` to the Field instead.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Text shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem, `lg` 2.75rem.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon before the value. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the select sizes it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Select label="Country" placeholder="Choose one" items={[{ value: "ar", label: "Argentina" }]} />
<Field label="Role" required><Select items={roles} /></Field>

components.name: Dialog
components.description:
Root of a modal dialog. Holds the open state; use `open` and `onOpenChange` to control it,
or `defaultOpen` to leave it uncontrolled. Built on Base UI Dialog (focus trap, Escape to close,
focus return and scroll lock come from there).
components.renders: no element: it only holds the open state (Base UI Dialog.Root)
components.composition: Structure: Dialog > DialogTrigger + DialogContent (title, description, DialogClose buttons).
components.whenToUse: Interrupting the user for a decision or focused task.
avoid: Non-essential information: use inline content or Tooltip.
Dialogs without a title.
Confirming destructive actions: use AlertDialog.
components.accessibility: Focus is trapped and returned, Escape closes, the page behind is inert. Title is the accessible name.
components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger>Delete project</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent title="Delete project?" description="This cannot be undone.">
    <DialogClose>Cancel</DialogClose>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

parts.name: DialogTrigger
parts.description: The button that opens the dialog. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Direct child of Dialog. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`.
parts.whenToUse: The button that opens the dialog.
avoid: Using a plain Button to open it.
parts.accessibility: Gets aria-haspopup and expanded state from Base UI.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <DialogTrigger>Open settings</DialogTrigger>

parts.name: DialogContent
parts.description:
The dialog panel with its backdrop, title and description.
Place it inside `Dialog`.
parts.renders: div role="dialog" in a portal, plus a backdrop
parts.composition: `title` is required; `description` is recommended. Children are the actions, usually DialogClose.
avoid: Omitting `title`.
parts.accessibility: title is the accessible name; description is the accessible description.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog title. Required: it is the accessible name of the dialog.

props.name: children
props.description: Body and actions. Put `DialogClose` buttons here.

props.name: description
props.description: Short explanation, announced as the accessible description.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<DialogContent title="Delete project?" description="This cannot be undone.">
  <DialogClose>Cancel</DialogClose>
</DialogContent>

parts.name: DialogClose
parts.description: A button that closes the dialog. It is rendered as a `Button`.
avoid: Closing by custom onClick state when DialogClose is enough.
parts.accessibility: Closing returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <DialogClose>Cancel</DialogClose>

components.name: AlertDialog
components.description:
Root of an alert dialog: a modal that asks for confirmation before a destructive or
irreversible action. It shares Dialog's panel styles but behaves like an alert dialog:
`role="alertdialog"`, no close on outside click, Escape to close, focus starts on the
safest action and returns to the trigger.
components.renders: no element: it only holds the open state (Base UI AlertDialog.Root)
components.composition: Structure: AlertDialog > AlertDialogTrigger + AlertDialogContent (title, description, AlertDialogClose actions). Put the safe action, usually Cancel, first.
components.whenToUse: Confirming a destructive or irreversible action before it runs, such as deleting data or leaving with unsaved changes.
avoid: Forms or general content: use Dialog.
Informational messages that need no decision: use Alert.
Confirmations whose action can be undone: use a Dialog or an inline action instead.
components.accessibility: Uses role="alertdialog"; it does not close on outside click, Escape closes, focus starts on the safe action and returns to the trigger. Title is the accessible name.
components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger variant="danger">Delete project</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent title="Delete project?" description="This cannot be undone.">
    <AlertDialogClose>Cancel</AlertDialogClose>
    <AlertDialogClose variant="danger">Delete</AlertDialogClose>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

parts.name: AlertDialogTrigger
parts.description: The button that opens the alert dialog. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Direct child of AlertDialog. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`; use `danger` for the destructive trigger.
parts.whenToUse: The button that opens the alert dialog.
avoid: Using a plain Button to open it.
parts.accessibility: Gets aria-haspopup and expanded state from Base UI.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <AlertDialogTrigger variant="danger">Delete project</AlertDialogTrigger>

parts.name: AlertDialogContent
parts.description:
The alert dialog panel with its backdrop, title and description. Place it inside
`AlertDialog`. It does not close on outside click, so the user must choose an action.
parts.renders: div role="alertdialog" in a portal, plus a backdrop
parts.composition: `title` is required; `description` is recommended. Children are the actions, usually AlertDialogClose. Put the safe action first: it receives initial focus.
parts.whenToUse: The panel of the alert dialog.
avoid: Omitting `title`.
Content other than the actions.
parts.accessibility: title is the accessible name; description is the accessible description. Initial focus goes to the first action unless `initialFocus` overrides it.

props.name: title
props.description: Dialog title. Required: it is the accessible name of the dialog.

props.name: children
props.description: The actions. Put the safe action first (`AlertDialogClose` buttons): it receives initial focus.

props.name: description
props.description: Short explanation of what will happen, announced as the accessible description.

props.name: initialFocus
props.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType: InteractionType) => boolean | void | HTMLElement | null)
props.description: Element to focus when the dialog opens. Defaults to the first action, which should be the safe one.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<AlertDialogContent title="Delete project?" description="This cannot be undone.">
  <AlertDialogClose>Cancel</AlertDialogClose>
  <AlertDialogClose variant="danger">Delete</AlertDialogClose>
</AlertDialogContent>

parts.name: AlertDialogClose
parts.description: A button that closes the alert dialog. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Inside AlertDialogContent. Accepts Button `variant` and `size`; use `danger` for the destructive action.
avoid: Closing by custom onClick state when AlertDialogClose is enough.
parts.accessibility: Closing returns focus to the trigger.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style. Use `danger` for the destructive action.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <AlertDialogClose>Cancel</AlertDialogClose>

components.name: Tooltip
components.description:
A small label that appears on hover or keyboard focus, built on Base UI Tooltip.
Tooltips do not appear on touch devices and are not a reliable way to describe a control, so use
them only to add clarity (for example the name of an icon button) and never for critical information.
components.renders: the child element as trigger; a popup div in a portal
components.composition: `content` is the text. The single child must be focusable and have its own accessible name.
components.whenToUse: Extra clarity for sighted mouse and keyboard users, such as naming an icon button.
avoid: Essential information: it does not appear on touch and is not linked to the trigger for screen readers.
Interactive content in the tooltip.
components.accessibility: Shows on hover and keyboard focus, hides on Escape. The trigger needs aria-label when it has no text.

props.name: children
props.description:
The element that triggers the tooltip. It must be focusable and already have its own
accessible name (visible text or `aria-label`).

props.name: content
props.description: Short supplementary text. Never put essential information only here.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Tooltip content="Bold"><Button aria-label="Bold" variant="ghost">B</Button></Tooltip>

components.name: Tabs
components.description:
Tabs that switch between panels, built on Base UI Tabs (arrow-key navigation, roles and
`aria-controls` come from there). Pass `items` instead of composing parts.
Tabs are compact: icons use the 16px small size.
components.renders: div with a tablist, tab buttons and tabpanels
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, label, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }) and an `aria-label`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; tabs are compact and use 16px icons.
components.whenToUse: Switching between related panels in the same place.
avoid: Navigation between pages: use Link.
Hiding content users must read.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys move between tabs; roles and aria-controls come from Base UI.

props.name: items
props.description: The tabs and their panels, in order.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tab list, for example "Account sections". Required when there is no visible heading for it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
Profile

}, { value: "billing", label: "Billing", content:

Billing

}, ]} />

components.name: ButtonLink
components.description:
A link that looks like a `Button`. It renders an `a` (or the component given to `LinkProvider`, such as
`next/link`), because something that navigates is a link, not a button. For actions use `Button`.
Put icons in `startIcon`/`endIcon`. They follow the control size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
An icon-only link is valid only with `startIcon` and an accessible name (`aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`); with visible children both icons are optional.
components.renders: a (rendered by the LinkProvider component, `next/link` in this app) styled like a Button
components.composition: Pass `href`, `variant`, `size` and optional `startIcon`/`endIcon` (generated icons, no `size`). Children are the visible label. Icon-only: `startIcon` is required and exactly one of `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Icons follow the size: sm 16px, md 20px, lg 24px.
components.whenToUse: A call to action that goes to another page, such as Get started or Docs.
avoid: Actions that do not navigate: use Button.
Inline links inside text: use Link (inline text).
components.accessibility: Icon-only buttons need `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`); the types enforce it. It is a real link (role link), so middle-click, open in new tab and prefetch work. Do not give it role button.

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes. Required.

props.name: children
props.description:
The visible label.
Icon-only links have no visible children.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon after the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the link sizes it.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: `sm` 1.75rem, `md` 2.25rem, `lg` 2.75rem.

props.name: startIcon
props.description:
Icon before the label. Pass a generated icon without `size`; the link sizes it.
The visible icon and accessible name. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual emphasis, the same as `Button`. `primary` is the main call to action (one per view).

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<ButtonLink href="/docs/installation">Get started</ButtonLink>
<ButtonLink href="/docs" variant="secondary" endIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />}>Docs</ButtonLink>
<ButtonLink href="/docs" aria-label="Next page" startIcon={<ArrowRightIcon />} />

components.name: Card
components.description:
A bordered container that groups related content. Its parts share one inset through
`--card-spacing`, and an `img` as the first child is full-bleed with rounded top corners.
components.renders: div by default; `as` can be article, section or li
components.composition: `CardHeader` (with `CardTitle`, optional `CardDescription` and `CardAction`) + `CardContent` + `CardFooter`. `size` sets the shared inset through `--card-spacing`; override that variable to use another spacing step. An `img` as the first child is full-bleed with rounded top corners.
components.whenToUse: Grouping related content in a bordered surface.
avoid: Making the whole card clickable: put a Link inside and keep the card as a container.
Nesting cards: use an `hr` hairline or a sunken region instead.
components.accessibility: A plain container with no role. Use `as="article"` for self-contained content and give it a heading through CardTitle.

props.name: as
props.description: Element to render. `article` for self-contained content, `section` for a named group.

props.name: size
props.description:
Inset between the card edge and its content. `sm` is 1rem, `default` is 1.5rem.
Override `--card-spacing` on the card to use another step of the spacing scale.

props.name: variant
props.description: `outline` draws only a soft border; `surface` adds the surface fill.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Card as="article" variant="surface">
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Release notes</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>What changed in this version.</CardDescription>
    <CardAction><Button variant="secondary">Share</Button></CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent><Text>Body of the card.</Text></CardContent>
  <CardFooter><Text size="sm" tone="muted">Updated today</Text></CardFooter>
</Card>

parts.name: CardHeader
parts.description:
The top region of a Card: a `CardTitle`, an optional `CardDescription` and an optional
`CardAction` at the top end.
parts.composition: Holds `CardTitle`, optional `CardDescription` and `CardAction`. The action aligns with the title at the top end.
parts.whenToUse: The title region of a Card.
avoid: Using it without a CardTitle.
parts.accessibility: No role of its own; the heading comes from CardTitle.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardTitle
parts.description:
The heading of a Card. Renders a real heading; the default `h3` suits a card inside a section
with an `h2`.
parts.renders: h3 by default; `as` sets the heading element
parts.composition: `as` sets the outline level (h2-h6) and `size` sets the look; it defaults to size 6.
avoid: Skipping heading levels to get a smaller look: change `size` instead.
parts.accessibility: A real heading, so it appears in the document outline.

props.name: as
props.description: Heading level in the document outline. Keep the order of the page.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size from 1 (largest) to 6 (smallest).

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardDescription
parts.description: Supporting text below a `CardTitle`, in the muted body style.
parts.whenToUse: Supporting text directly under the card title.
avoid: Long prose: put it in CardContent.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardAction
parts.description: A control at the top end of a Card, aligned with `CardTitle`.
parts.composition: Holds a Button, ButtonLink or Badge at the top end of `CardHeader`, aligned with the title.
parts.whenToUse: A control that belongs to the whole card.
avoid: Hiding the card title to make room for the action.
parts.accessibility: Adds no semantics; the control inside needs its own accessible name.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardContent
parts.description: The main content region of a Card, aligned with the header and footer.
parts.composition: The main body between `CardHeader` and `CardFooter`, aligned with both.
avoid: Repeating the header or footer content.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

parts.name: CardFooter
parts.description: The bottom region of a Card, aligned with the header and content.
parts.composition: The bottom region for metadata or actions, aligned with the header and content.
parts.whenToUse: Metadata or closing actions at the bottom of a Card.
avoid: Putting the only primary action at the bottom when CardAction would do.
parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.

components.name: Alert
components.description:
An inline message about the state of the page or a form. `danger` and `warning` use `role="alert"`
(announced immediately); `info` and `success` use `role="status"` (announced politely).
For short-lived feedback after an action, use `useToast` instead.
components.renders: div with role alert (danger, warning) or role status (info, success)
components.composition: Pass `tone`, optional `title`, and the message as children. `startIcon` replaces the tone glyph; `endIcon` adds a trailing icon (generated icons, no `size`; the single-size alert uses 20px icons).
components.whenToUse: A message that stays on the page and the user must notice, such as a failed save or a warning.
avoid: Short-lived confirmations: use Toast.
Using color alone: the tone also changes the icon and you should say it in the text.
Confirming a destructive action: use AlertDialog.
components.accessibility: Announced by screen readers on render. The icon is decorative and each tone has a different shape.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: Icon at the end, for example a link arrow. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Replaces the tone icon at the start. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: title
props.description: Short heading of the message.

props.name: tone
props.description: Meaning of the message. It changes the icon shape as well as the color, so it never relies on color alone.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Alert tone="danger" title="Payment failed">Check your card details and try again.</Alert>

Icons use the 20px medium size (the alert has no size variants).

components.name: Avatar
components.description:
A round image of a person with an initials fallback, built on Base UI Avatar.
The whole avatar is one image with the person's name as its label. Add a status, badge or icon
fallback when needed; without them the markup and accessible name stay just the name.
components.renders: span with role img and the name as aria-label
components.composition: Pass `name` (required), `src` and `size`; initials are the fallback. `status` adds a shape at the bottom end and appends the state to the name; `badge` with `badgeLabel` adds a custom icon and appends its label; `icon` replaces the initials. `status` and `badge` cannot be combined. Every feature scales with `size`.
components.whenToUse: Showing who a person or account is.
avoid: Using it as a button: wrap it in a Button or Link.
Omitting `name`.
Combining `status` and `badge`: they are mutually exclusive.
components.accessibility: The name is the accessible name. A status appends the state, and a badge appends `badgeLabel`, such as "Ada Lovelace, online" or "Ada Lovelace, Verified". Initials, icon, status shape and badge are hidden from assistive technology; status is never color alone.

props.name: name
props.description: Full name of the person or entity. It is the accessible name and the source of the initials. Required.

props.name: badge
props.description: Custom badge icon at the bottom end. Pass a generated icon without `size`. Cannot be combined with `status`.

props.name: badgeLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the badge. Required with `badge`; appended to the accessible name.

props.name: icon
props.description: Replaces the initials fallback with an icon, for bots or organizations. Pass a generated icon without `size`.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter: `sm` 2rem, `md` 2.5rem, `lg` 3.5rem.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. If it is missing or fails to load, the initials are shown.

props.name: status
props.description: Presence state. Appended to the accessible name, such as "Ada Lovelace, online". Cannot be combined with `badge`.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src="/ada.png" />
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" status="online" />
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" badge={<CheckIcon />} badgeLabel="Verified" />
<Avatar name="Build bot" icon={<TerminalWindowIcon />} />

parts.name: AvatarGroup
parts.description:
Overlapping avatars that share one size. When there are more than `max`, the extra avatars
collapse into a "+N" item labelled "and N more". Used outside a group, Avatar is unchanged.
parts.renders: div role="group" with overlapping Avatar elements
parts.composition: Pass `children` (Avatar elements), `max` (default 4) and shared `size` (default md). Avatars beyond `max` collapse into a visible "+N" item labelled "and N more".
parts.whenToUse: A compact summary of several people or accounts.
avoid: One avatar: use Avatar directly.
Long lists where every person matters: show them in a list.
parts.accessibility: The group has role="group"; give it an `aria-label`. Each avatar keeps its own name, and the overflow item is announced as "and N more".

props.name: children
props.description: Avatars in the group. They share the group's `size`.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars stay visible before the rest collapse into a "+N" item.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter shared by every avatar in the group.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<AvatarGroup max={3} aria-label="Project members">
  <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" />
  <Avatar name="Grace Hopper" />
  <Avatar name="Alan Turing" />
  <Avatar name="Katherine Johnson" />
</AvatarGroup>

components.name: Popover
components.description:
Root of a popover: a small panel anchored to a button, for extra controls or details the user asked for.
Built on Base UI Popover (focus management, Escape to close, outside click and positioning come from there).
For decisions that must interrupt the user use `Dialog`; for a list of actions use `Menu`.
components.renders: no element: it only holds the open state (Base UI Popover.Root)
components.composition: Structure: Popover > PopoverTrigger + PopoverContent (title required, description optional, PopoverClose).
components.whenToUse: Small interactive content tied to a button, such as a form or extra options.
avoid: Plain hints: use Tooltip.
Blocking decisions: use Dialog.
components.accessibility: Focus moves into the popup and Escape closes it. Title is the accessible name.
components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger variant="secondary">Filters</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent title="Filters" description="Narrow the results.">...</PopoverContent>
</Popover>

parts.name: PopoverTrigger
parts.description: The button that opens the popover. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Child of Popover. Accepts Button props.
parts.whenToUse: The button that opens a Popover.
avoid: Using it outside Popover.
parts.accessibility: A real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <PopoverTrigger variant="secondary">Filters</PopoverTrigger>

parts.name: PopoverContent
parts.description: The popover panel with its title and description. Place it inside `Popover`.
parts.renders: div with role dialog in a portal, with a title
parts.composition: Child of Popover. Requires `title`; `description`, `side` and `align` are optional.
parts.whenToUse: The panel shown by a Popover.
avoid: Leaving out the title.
parts.accessibility: Labelled by its title. Focus is returned to the trigger on close.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the panel. Required: it is the accessible name of the popover.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment against the trigger.

props.name: children
props.description: The content: text, a form, or `PopoverClose` buttons.

props.name: description
props.description: Short explanation, announced as the accessible description.

props.name: side
props.description: Preferred side of the trigger.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<PopoverContent title="Filters" description="Narrow the results.">
  <PopoverClose>Done</PopoverClose>
</PopoverContent>

parts.name: PopoverClose
parts.description: A button that closes the popover. It is rendered as a `Button`.
parts.composition: Inside PopoverContent. Children are the label.
parts.whenToUse: A button that closes the Popover.
avoid: Icon-only without a label.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style.

parts.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <PopoverClose>Done</PopoverClose>

components.name: Menu
components.description:
A dropdown list of actions or links, built on Base UI Menu (arrow keys, typeahead, focus return and
Escape come from there). Items with `href` are real links; items with `onSelect` are actions.
Do not put form controls in a menu: use `Popover`. The trigger icons follow its button size;
menu items are compact and use 16px icons.
components.renders: button that opens a role menu with menuitems
components.composition: Pass `label` (the button text) and `items`: `{ label, startIcon?, endIcon?, onSelect?, href?, disabled?, destructive? }` or `{ type: "separator" }`. Icons are generated icons without `size`; the trigger follows its button size and menu items are compact (16px).
components.whenToUse: A list of actions or links behind one button, such as account actions.
avoid: Navigation between sections of the site: use links.
Form choices: use Select.
components.accessibility: Arrow keys, Home, End, typeahead and Escape come from Base UI. Items with `href` are real links.

props.name: items
props.description: Items in order. Use `{ type: "separator" }` to group them.

props.name: label
props.description: Text of the button that opens the menu.

props.name: align
props.description: Alignment of the menu against the trigger.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size of the trigger.

props.name: variant
props.description: Button style of the trigger.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Menu label="Account" items={[
  { label: "Profile", href: "/profile" },
  { type: "separator" },
  { label: "Sign out", onSelect: signOut },
]} />

components.name: Accordion
components.description:
Collapsible sections built on Base UI Accordion. Each title is a button inside an `h3`
(`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` come from Base UI). Pass `items` instead of composing parts.
components.renders: div with a heading (h3) and button per item and a region per panel
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ value, title, content, startIcon?, endIcon?, disabled? }). Icons are generated icons without `size`. Use `multiple` to allow several open.
components.whenToUse: Showing long content in short sections, such as FAQs.
avoid: Hiding content users must read.
Navigation between pages.
components.accessibility: Each title is a button in a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, in order.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Ids of the panels open at first.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow several panels open at once.

props.name: value
props.description: Ids of the open panels, when you control it.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
Yes.

}, { value: "b", title: "Is it themeable?", content:

Yes.

}, ]} />

components.name: Table
components.description:
Data table with a real `table`, `caption`, `th scope="col"` and a first-column row header. The wrapper
scrolls horizontally on small screens and is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
For layout, use `Grid` or `Stack`, never a table.
components.renders: table with caption, thead, tbody, th scope and a focusable scroll region
components.composition: Pass `caption`, `columns` ({ key, header, align? }) and `rows` (objects by key). Use `align: "end"` for numeric columns: they align end and use tabular numbers.
components.whenToUse: Comparing data across rows and columns.
avoid: Page layout: use Grid or Stack.
Missing caption.
components.accessibility: Real table semantics. The first column is a row header. The scroll wrapper is focusable and named.

props.name: caption
props.description: Describes the table. Required: it is the accessible name and the visible caption.

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions, in order.

props.name: rows
props.description: One object per row, keyed by `columns[].key`.

props.name: hideCaption
props.description: Visually hide the caption (it stays available to screen readers).

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Key of the row value that is unique per row. Falls back to the row index.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples:
<Table caption="Plans" columns={[{ key: "name", header: "Plan" }, { key: "price", header: "Price", align: "end" }]}
  rows={[{ name: "Free", price: "$0" }, { name: "Pro", price: "$12" }]} />

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description:
Where the current page sits in the site. Renders `nav > ol` and marks the last item with
`aria-current="page"`. Links use whatever `LinkProvider` provides (`next/link` in this app).
components.renders: nav with an ordered list; the last item has aria-current page
components.composition: Pass `items` ({ label, href?, startIcon?, endIcon? }) from root to current page. Icons are generated icons without `size`.
components.whenToUse: Showing where the page sits in the site.
avoid: Primary navigation.
Linking the last item.
components.accessibility: nav labelled Breadcrumb; the current page is marked with aria-current.

props.name: items
props.description: The trail from the root to the current page. The last item is marked as the current page.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation. Change it when a page has more than one breadcrumb.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "Docs", href: "/docs" }, { label: "Components", href: "/docs/components" }, { label: "Button" }]} />

components.name: Pagination
components.description:
Page links for content split across URLs. Every page is a real link, so it works without JavaScript and
with `next/link` through `LinkProvider`. Previous and next are left out (not disabled) when unavailable.
components.renders: nav with a list of links
components.composition: Pass `page`, `pageCount` and `hrefTemplate` such as `/blog?page={page}`.
components.whenToUse: Moving through content split across URLs.
avoid: Passing a function for the href (it breaks in Server Components).
Infinite lists.
components.accessibility: Every page is a link; the current one has aria-current. Previous and Next are removed, not disabled, when unavailable.

props.name: hrefTemplate
props.description: URL of a page, with `{page}` where the number goes, for example `"/blog?page={page}"`. A string (not a function) so it works from Server Components.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, starting at 1.

props.name: pageCount
props.description: Total number of pages.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the navigation.

components.extends: Also accepts the native props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Pagination page={2} pageCount={9} hrefTemplate="/blog?page={page}" />

components.name: Progress
components.description:
Progress of a task, built on Base UI Progress (`role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`).
For a quick wait with no known end, prefer `Spinner`; for a value the user sets, use `Slider`.
components.renders: div with role progressbar
components.composition: Pass `label` and `value` (number, or null when unknown). Optional `max`.
components.whenToUse: Showing how far a task has got.
avoid: Values the user sets: use Slider.
Short unknown waits: use Spinner.
components.accessibility: role progressbar with aria-valuenow; the label is the accessible name.

props.name: label
props.description: What is progressing. Required: it is the accessible name.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. Use `null` when the amount is unknown (indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum value.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the percentage next to the label.

components.extends: Also accepts the native/Base UI props of the element it renders; they pass through.
examples: <Progress label="Uploading" value={40} />

components.name: Slider
components.description:
Pick a number, or a range, by dragging or with arrow keys. Built on Base UI Slider (each thumb is an
`input type="range"`). For a short list of exact choices use `Select`; for typing a number, use `Input`.
Inside `Field` it inherits `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading`.
components.renders: div with one input type range per thumb
components.composition: Pass `label` and `defaultValue` (number or [min, max]). Use `thumbLabels` for ranges. Accepts `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `loading` directly, or inherits them from Field.
components.whenToUse: Choosing a number or range by dragging.
avoid: Exact entry: use Input.
A few named options: use Select.
components.accessibility: Each thumb is a native range input with arrow-key support. The label is the accessible name. Invalid uses the danger border and an error linked with aria-describedby; required prints Required; read-only stays focusable and blocks changes; loading sets aria-busy and blocks changes.

props.name: label
props.description: What the slider sets. Required: it is the accessible name.

props.name: data-force
props.description: Story/test hook: force the focus ring without moving focus.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value, or `[min, max]` for a range.

props.name: error
props.description:
Error message. Marks the slider invalid and links the message with `aria-describedby`.
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `error` to the Field instead.

props.name: loading
props.description:
Shows a small spinner next to the value, sets `aria-busy`, and makes the slider not
interactive.

props.name: readOnly
props.description:
The slider can be focused and read but not changed. Uses the sunken track and keeps the
label at full contrast. Distinct from `disabled`.

props.name: required
props.description:
The slider must have a value before the form can be submitted. The label prints "Required".
Inside `Field`, omit it and pass `required` to the Field instead.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the current value next to the label.

props.name: thumbLabels
